correctness.rationale: The precise time-dependent Bernoulli law is immediate from independent uniform recruiter choices. Uniform Cramer-Chernoff upper and tilted lower bounds give exponent I_u(x). For distinct vertices, conditional competition yields negative covariance of threshold exceedance indicators; hence second-moment lower bounds hold despite dependence. The concave exponent Phi(u,x) has a unique global saddle, giving both the deterministic age frontier and the maximizing birth exponent. Subsequence Borel-Cantelli and monotonicity yield almost-sure frontier convergence. The actual 11,030 exact/numerical checks support, but do not replace, these analytic steps.

value.rationale: A newly defined simultaneous-batch growth model has an exact nontrivial degree-age frontier, global maximum child-degree coefficient \(m/\log(m+1)\), and unique hub birth exponent. These are canonical hub-formation observables, distinguish synchronous siblings from multi-parent-edge growth, and require handling dependent competing recruiters. The result gives a structural transition across the full continuum of birth cutoffs, not a routine fixed-degree urn calculation.
